newsitem.title: PERU: Peru guerrillas attack public buildings in Andes.
newsitem.headline: Peru guerrillas attack public buildings in Andes.

text.p: More than a score of heavily armed Peruvian guerrillas swarmed through an isolated village in the northern Andes and attacked public buildings with explosives, police said on Wednesday.

The rebels caused damage to the village hall, the local governor's house and a small clinic but did not injure anybody at Buldibuyo in the region of La Libertad, regional police told Reuters by telephone.

Officials said they did not know which rebel group was responsible for the attack that ocurred in the early hours on Tuesday, three days travel by jeep from the region's police headquarters at Trujillo, 360 miles (570 km) north of Lima.
National radio station CPN reported that Maoist Shining Path members carried out the attack and stole food from the village before rushing off to their hideouts.

For two weeks, Peru's security forces have been sweeping through neighbouring departments along the Huallaga valley in a massive operation to flush Shining Path military leaders out of their jungle strongholds.

In recent months, Peru's smaller rebel group Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) overshadowed Shining Path with a dramatic hostage-taking at the Japanese ambassador's home in Lima. But since last month's bloody end to the siege the Shining Path has carried out several attacks, raising fears of a new campaign of violence.
